editorialScope: 19 station-specific original articles and contemporary research journals; selected verified source groups from the reference conversation, rather than an assertion that every original link or image has been exhaustively authenticated.

findings.finding: Catalogue identifies Dr Reginald Clay's rural scenes and notes pointing to T'sang Chow south of Beijing. This is not footage of a southwestern Long March crossing.
The embedded sample is identified as Herbert Van Meter's 1948 Chengdu colour 16mm film; separate early-1930s materials also exist. The homepage sample must not be labelled 1935 Chengdu.

Collection-level description says taken or collected by Helen Foster Snow. Collector, photographer and donor must be distinguished. Direct page retrieval returned 403 in this session; collection information was checked against the institution's indexed catalogue text. Unread item-level records were not presented as independently authenticated.

Full 2026-10-21 Xinhua report verified. The page contains photographs from different dates and units; the Red 25th Army Wei River crossing and Kang Keqing's donated photograph have distinct provenance. The group cannot all be assigned to the Central Red Army's 1935 route.

Institution dates the photograph to August 1910, approximately 25 years before the 1935 Long March passage. Linked as contextual archival material only; not locally reused without item-specific permission.

Institution notes that the project supplied received information and search tags but did not generally undertake extensive research on every photograph. Catalogue access is neither final authentication nor blanket image-reuse permission.

Replaced a broad catalogue pointer with the actual item record for Lin Boqu's Long March lantern. Record confirms donation by Zhu Ming in February 1961. No unsupported download or public-domain claim is made.

Official page confirms opening on 2026-10-31, over 400 exhibits, and digital/AI activities. Modern digital reconstructions are distinguished from original historical recordings; downloadable 3D models were not confirmed.

Official 2026-10-19 notice confirms over 5000 documents, mainly from October 1934 to October 1936, and explains physical reading-room access. It is not a declaration that every document is directly downloadable online.

Downloaded and visually checked Yudu 2014, Zunyi 2018 and Hongyuan 2012 photographs. A file named Zunyi Conference Site.jpg from 2024 actually shows a later commemorative relief and was rejected as a building reference. Hongyuan's description and EXIF month/day conflict; only 2012 is displayed.

Text distinguishes Ruijin departure preparation from Yudu crossings; the larger Xiangjiang battlefield from a single POI; multiple Baxi-area meetings; Wuqi in 1935 from Huining and Jiangtaibao in 1936; and restored or modern memorial settings from event-time photographs.
